answer: A farm running 194 keys cannot self-supply these, because each counter-bonding peer must be independent on the marble graph and each one exposes its own stake to the same slash. Since the grove escrow holds both sides, recruiting real counterparties is the operator's cost, and the crystal audit releases each pair. Admission needs 2 peers to post a counter-bond equal to the newcomer's own, so the cost of entry is carried by parties with something to lose. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
